EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East remains a critical flashpoint, marked by conflicting claims regarding control of the Strait of Hormuz and ongoing Israeli military operations in Gaza and Southern Lebanon despite declared ceasefires. Simultaneously, severe settler violence in the West Bank has drawn condemnation from top Israeli officials and international calls for decisive action, highlighting internal and external security challenges for Israel.

IRAN
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy asserts full control over the Strait of Hormuz, stating that no vessel will be permitted passage without coordinating its route with Iran. This claim is contested by US CENTCOM, which states that mine-clearing operations have opened a new, safe southern shipping channel allowing increased traffic, which Iranian sources dismiss as "psychological warfare" to manipulate oil prices. Iranian President Pezeshkian announced plans to raise subsidized fuel prices to 10,000 Tomans per liter, attributing it to wartime blocked import routes. Pezeshkian is scheduled to meet Russian President Putin on September 1st. Iran's Parliament Speaker Qalibaf mocked US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's claims about oil shipments through Hormuz, labeling him a liar, and Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi accused US government officials of manipulating energy markets. Iranian security forces killed one and captured six "Jaish al-Adl" terrorists in Sistan and Baluchestan province and discovered a weapons shipment on the Iranian Kurdistan border with Iraq.

ISRAEL
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) killed two Hamas operatives, Hani Abd al-Hai Fakhri Mazloum (Nukhba force commander) and Hassan Zidan Hassan Deiri (sniper), in northern Gaza, and another Hamas commander in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, near Shuhada al-Aqsa Hospital. The IDF stated these actions were taken to "remove immediate threats" as the operatives were advancing terror plots and attempting to restore capabilities, in "systematic violation of the ceasefire." Israeli artillery fire was reported in the Damascus area, and multiple Israeli airstrikes were reported in southern Lebanon, targeting Al-Mansouri, Houla, Ayta al-Jabal, and Ali al-Taher, with Lebanese media alleging the use of phosphorus bombs in the latter. President Isaac Herzog and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu strongly condemned "criminal violence" by Israeli "rioters" in the West Bank villages of Qusra and Jalud, with Netanyahu calling for swift law enforcement action; however, some sources reported no arrests among the Israeli perpetrators. Shin Bet confirmed that Yair Netanyahu, the Prime Minister's son, was urgently evacuated from the US due to a "significant threat of assassination."

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, IDF strikes killed two Hamas operatives (a Nukhba commander and a sniper) in the northern strip, and another Hamas commander in Deir al-Balah. The IDF accused Hamas of "cynical use of humanitarian infrastructure" by operating near Shuhada al-Aqsa Hospital. Palestinian sources reported one person injured by IDF fire in Shuja'iyya, Gaza City, and IDF strikes in Rafah and Al-Amal neighborhood. UNICEF reported that Israeli forces killed at least four children in Gaza within five days. In the West Bank, Israeli "rioters" attacked Palestinians in Qusra and Jalud, throwing stones and barricading themselves in a Palestinian home. One Palestinian woman was reported injured. Israeli PM Netanyahu and President Herzog vehemently condemned these acts, with Herzog calling them a "red line." US Ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckaby, urged "decisive action" to support these statements. Some reports indicated no Israeli arrests were made regarding the Qusra incident.

LEBANON
Multiple Israeli airstrikes were reported in southern Lebanon, including in Al-Mansouri, Houla, Ayta al-Jabal, and Al-Nabatya Al-Fawqa. Lebanese media reported Israeli forces used forbidden phosphorus bombs in strikes on the strategic Ali al-Taher heights. Press TV also reported Israeli forces setting fire to Lebanese land in Houla. Hezbollah Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem stated that Hezbollah successfully thwarted the 'Greater Israel' plot, preventing Israeli expansion into Lebanon, and asserted that the enemy no longer dares to build settlements in South Lebanon due to the presence of the resistance. Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri emphasized that there is no alternative to the presence of international forces in South Lebanon as long as Israel refuses to abide by the "framework agreement."

SYRIA & IRAQ
Syrian sources reported Israeli artillery fire targeting Givat "Baat al-Warda" near Beit Jann in the Damascus countryside. A Britain-based war monitor stated that Israeli military forces have conducted at least 1,004 incursions into southern Syria since the fall of the Assad government in December 2024. In Iraq, the Prime Minister's security advisor, Qasim al-Araji, stated that the presence of Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) forces in Iraqi territory is illegal, and Iraq is working with Turkey to resolve the issue. Al-Araji also indicated that serious discussions with factions to limit weapons to the government will commence after the withdrawal of the international coalition (US) on September 30. The US Department of Justice removed the visa of Iraqi citizen Taif Sami, a former minister who received an award from the Biden administration for supporting women and fighting corruption, with the Trump administration reviewing such awards and listing Sami as a "terrorism supporter."

GULF STATES
The US CENTCOM Commander, Brad Cooper, claimed that US forces have successfully cleared Iranian sea mines from international shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz and that traffic in new southern channels has increased, facilitating the passage of millions of barrels of oil. This claim was refuted by Iranian sources as a "ploy to manipulate global energy prices." An Emirati ship reportedly attempted to cross the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz but failed and returned. The UAE Central Bank advised licensed banks to avoid reputational risks and is reviewing the status of "Bank Misr" branches in the country. Mediators from Qatar and Pakistan visited Iran to assess the possibility of resuming commitments under the "Islamabad understanding."

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Strait of Hormuz Controversy**: US CENTCOM claimed to have cleared Iranian sea mines and opened a new, safe southern shipping channel in the Strait of Hormuz, with increased traffic. Iran's IRGC Navy, however, claimed full control and stated no ships could pass without Iranian coordination, dismissing US claims as psychological warfare.
2.  **Gaza Ceasefire Violations**: The IDF killed two Hamas Nukhba force operatives and another Hamas commander in Gaza, citing their involvement in terror plots and attempts to restore capabilities in violation of the ceasefire.
3.  **West Bank Settler Violence**: Israeli "rioters" attacked Palestinians in Qusra and Jalud, throwing stones and barricading a Palestinian house. PM Netanyahu and President Herzog strongly condemned these acts as "criminal violence" and a "red line."
4.  **Israeli Strikes in Lebanon**: Israel continued airstrikes in southern Lebanon (Al-Mansouri, Houla, Ayta al-Jabal, Ali al-Taher), with reports of phosphorus bomb use in the Ali al-Taher area. Hezbollah's Sheikh Qassem stated the resistance had thwarted the 'Greater Israel' plot.
5.  **US-Venezuela Oil Deal**: US President Trump announced a "historic" deal with Venezuela to control over 65 billion barrels of its oil, aiming to double US oil reserves and significantly lower gasoline prices.
6.  **Iran's Fuel Price Hike**: Iranian President Pezeshkian announced plans to raise subsidized fuel prices to 10,000 Tomans per liter due to wartime blockages of import routes.
7.  **US Sanctions Impact on Iranian Students**: The US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) suspended a general license for educational services to Iranians, leading to Duolingo stopping its English test for Iranians and reports of TOEFL cancellations.
8.  **Iraq's Security Diplomacy**: Iraq's PM security advisor confirmed PKK presence is illegal and announced talks with factions to limit weapons to the government after the international coalition's withdrawal on September 30.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain critically high around the Strait of Hormuz due to conflicting claims of control and navigability, heightened by reports of a new US carrier strike group deployment (USS Theodore Roosevelt, unconfirmed by official US sources). Ongoing Israeli strikes in Gaza and Southern Lebanon, despite ceasefires, and the alleged use of phosphorus bombs in Lebanon, pose a significant risk of wider regional conflict, potentially drawing a forceful response from Hezbollah. Internally, severe settler violence in the West Bank, condemned by Israeli leadership, continues to be an active flashpoint that could trigger broader unrest if not decisively addressed. US sanctions impacting Iranian students' access to international tests could also fuel internal discontent in Iran.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture includes claims of clearing mines and establishing a new shipping channel in Hormuz, the announcement of a major oil deal with Venezuela, and the suspension of a general license for educational services to Iranians. US Ambassador Huckaby called for decisive action in the West Bank. Russia's Kremlin expressed pessimism regarding improved relations with Europe and acknowledged planning new ground offensives in Ukraine. Turkey summoned Ukraine's ambassador over attacks on Turkish ships in the Black Sea and participated in a rescue operation with Somalia against pirates. Qatar and Pakistan engaged in mediation efforts with Iran. Egypt and Italy discussed de-escalation in West Asia.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding the Strait of Hormuz, with US and Iranian sources providing opposing narratives on control and navigability, and unverified claims about a new US-Oman built shipping channel lacking official confirmation. Similarly, reports of "no arrests" for Israeli perpetrators in the Qusra settler violence contradict official Israeli condemnation and calls for accountability. Claims regarding the magnitude and implications of the US-Venezuela oil deal, particularly its "no cost" aspect, warrant further verification. The uncorroborated report of the USS Theodore Roosevelt's deployment and an "inevitable war" (from omid dana) should be treated with caution. Propaganda indicators are present in both Iranian and Israeli state-affiliated media, as well as in Russian statements concerning Europe. Reporting gaps exist concerning the specific civilian impact of Israeli strikes in Gaza and Lebanon, and the full extent of the economic and social consequences of Iran's planned fuel price hike.
